transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… mostly I’m just really tired. Like, I know everyone gets tired, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my body feels completely drained. Even walking in from my car to the clinic felt like a lot, and at work, just opening the EHR can feel like it takes everything I have.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to sound like I’m complaining or anything, but after all that energy kind of dropped off, I started feeling really empty most days. Like… hopeless, I guess. Like I already messed up my chance at a future in healthcare before it even really started. Does that make sense?
After you do something small, like walking in from the car, do you feel significantly worse afterward?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but yes, even small stuff seems to wipe me out. Like walking in from my car to here, I felt completely drained after, and at work even just opening the EHR can feel like it takes everything I have. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
When you wake up after a full night of sleep, do you still feel unrefreshed?

Yeah… I do. I mean, it’s kind of inconsistent, but lately even if I sleep a lot — like, half the day sometimes — I still wake up feeling exhausted, not really rested. Or I’ll wake up before dawn and feel sick with worry.

There was also a period where I was only sleeping like two or three hours and somehow still felt wired, which… I know probably sounds bad. But right now it’s more like I just don’t wake up feeling refreshed at all.
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours and still felt wired, did you feel unusually energized or euphoric?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I was trying to be dramatic or anything, but some days I felt really good. Like… amazing, honestly. Kind of unstoppable, like I could handle everything and didn’t need to slow down.

But then if someone corrected my documentation or told me I needed to take it easier, I’d get really irritated. I snapped at people like they were insulting me, even if they probably weren’t. I’m not proud of that. Is that what you mean by unusually energized?
During that time, were you more active than usual or taking on a lot more projects than normal?

Yeah… I guess I was. I thought of it more like I was just trying to be helpful, but I started making all these workflow plans and messaging coworkers after hours with ideas.

I also offered to train people, even though honestly I was barely ahead of them myself. And I kept picking up extra tasks… like, more than I could really handle. It got to the point where I was having trouble finishing the basic stuff safely, which I’m embarrassed to say. Does that answer what you mean?
About that time when you felt wired and unusually good, how many days in a row did that last?

Um… it’s hard to pin it down exactly day by day. It wasn’t just, like, one weekend. The whole thing kind of built up over maybe two months after the clinic changed what I was responsible for.

I know that probably sounds like a long time… but it wasn’t the same intensity every single day, if that makes sense. It sort of escalated over that period.
During that wired period, did it cause serious problems at work or lead other people to step in because of your behavior?

Yeah… I mean, I wanted to think it was just stress or me trying too hard, but it did start causing real problems.

I got to where I couldn’t finish my documentation safely, and I wasn’t staying focused enough on the patient-support tasks. I hate saying that, because I really do care about doing the job right. But employee health ended up pulling me from work and sending me for an emergency evaluation.

And I had to stop really preparing for my CNA certification too, because I just couldn’t keep up with it at that point. Does that make sense?
During that wired period, did you ever hear or see things that other people said weren’t there?

Um… yeah, a little. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but during shifts I’d hear my name over the clinic speaker sometimes, or like a monitor beeping like it was for me.

And then I’d go looking for a patient or a call that… wasn’t actually happening, I guess. Other people would say they didn’t hear anything. I felt really embarrassed about it, honestly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Were you hospitalized during that wired period?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that… I don’t think I was, like, admitted overnight or anything that I remember. I was sent for an emergency evaluation, but hospitalization… I don’t think so.

Is that what you mean, like actually staying in the hospital?
During that wired period, did you have any beliefs that other people said were not true?

Yeah… I guess there was something like that. I don’t want to sound arrogant or anything, because normally I know I’m just learning and trying to do my part.

But at the time I got really convinced that I’d been, like… chosen to fix how the whole clinic took care of patients. It felt really important, like I had this mission. And even when my supervisor told me I was just an aide in training and that wasn’t my role, I still felt like they were trying to stop me or block what I was supposed to do.

I know that probably sounds strange now. Is that the kind of belief you mean?
Did you ever hear things or have those strong mission-like beliefs at a time when you were not feeling unusually energized or wired?

I don’t think so, no. I mean… not that I can remember.

The hearing my name or thinking the monitors were kind of “for me,” and that whole feeling like I had this special medical mission — that was only when I was really wired and barely sleeping, trying to fix everything at the clinic. Once that period calmed down, I wasn’t hearing those things or feeling chosen like that anymore.

That’s the best way I can describe it, if that makes sense.
